chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding the egg of the ostrich, the expiation is one sheep; if he cannot find one, then fasting for three days; and whoever cannot do that, his expiation is feeding ten poor people, when it befalls him while he is in the state of Ihram. And regarding the egg of the sandgrouse, it is obligatory that he release male sheep to mate with females in the number of the eggs; whatever is produced is a sacrifice (hady) for the House of Allah, the Exalted. It was narrated.

key_terms.كَفَّارَتُهُ: Expiation or compensation for a ritual violation
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.هَدْيًا: A sacrificial animal offered during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for accidentally killing an ostrich or sandgrouse while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the proportional expiation (kaffarah) for accidentally killing specific birds while in Ihram, reflecting the juristic principle of *qiyas* (analogical reasoning) applied to avian species. It distinguishes between the fixed penalty for the ostrich egg and the generative penalty for the sandgrouse, where the offspring of the matched livestock serve as the *had'y* (sacrifice) for the Kaaba.
